S001.name: Detail_Inattention_Errors
S001.description: Often fails to give close attention to details or makes careless mistakes.
examples: Makes mistakes in homework or tests by misreading questions or skipping important parts.
Frequently omits details or makes typos in work documents or reports.
Repeats mistakes in calculations or numerical work, such as switching signs or getting digits wrong.
Performs tasks incorrectly by missing important details in instructions.

S002.name: Sustained_Attention_Difficulty
S002.description: Often has difficulty sustaining attention in tasks or play activities.
examples: Focuses at first during class or meetings but soon becomes distracted or spaces out.
Re-reads the same paragraph in a book multiple times but the content does not register.
Loses focus while watching movies or TV and misses the plot.
Unable to maintain attention until the end of a long meeting or lecture, often drifting off or becoming drowsy.

S004.name: Instruction_Follow through_Difficulty
S004.description: Often does not follow through on instructions and fails to finish schoolwork, chores, or duties in the workplace.
examples: Starts homework or projects but fails to complete them, submitting unfinished work or missing deadlines.
When given multi-step instructions, follows only the first few steps and forgets the rest.
Starts cleaning or organizing but switches to another task midway, failing to finish.
Leaves almost completed work reports or paperwork unfinished, neglecting the final steps.

S008.name: Distractibility
S008.description: Often easily distracted by extraneous stimuli (for older adolescents and adults, may include unrelated thoughts).
examples: Easily distracted and stops working due to small noises or movements nearby.
Cannot concentrate because eyes keep wandering to the scenery outside the window or people passing by.
Starts daydreaming or gets sidetracked by sudden thoughts while working or studying.
Loses focus and listens in when hearing side conversations or TV sounds.

S009.name: Daily_Activities_Forgetfulness
S009.description: Often forgetful in daily activities (e.g., doing chores, running errands; for older adolescents and adults, returning calls, paying bills, keeping appointments).
examples: Forgets appointment times or meeting schedules, arriving late or missing them entirely.
Forgets to reply to received calls or messages for days.
Frequently incurs late fees because of missing deadlines for utility bills or credit card payments.
Forgets to take medication or leaves necessary items at home when going out.

S010.name: Fidgeting
S010.description: Often fidgets with or taps hands or feet or squirms in seat.
examples: Constantly shaking legs or twisting and squirming body while seated.
Spinning a pen or fiddling with nearby objects, unable to keep hands still.
Continually changing posture and feeling uncomfortable while sitting.
Constantly moving, such as tapping the desk with fingers or tapping feet on the floor.

S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
examples: Feels uncomfortable and restless as if something is squirming inside when sitting still.
Feels internally anxious and stifled in situations requiring prolonged sitting.
A sense of urgency and anxiety that one must keep moving or doing something.
Feels unable to endure staying still and must constantly be doing something.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
examples: Unable to engage in calm activities for long, such as reading quietly or drawing.
Cannot play quietly, often shouting or making loud noises during games or play.
Unable to stay quiet in quiet places like libraries or movie theaters, making noise.
Cannot endure and avoids quiet and calm activities like meditation or yoga.

S014.name: Constant_Activity
S014.description: Is often 'on the go', acting as if 'driven by a motor'.
examples: Constantly moving and active as if driven by a motor.
Starts another task immediately after finishing one, without resting for a moment.
Unable to stay still even on weekends or days off, constantly doing something.
Appears to others to be always busy and bustling about.

S017.name: Waiting_Turn_Difficulty
S017.description: Often has difficulty waiting his or her turn.
examples: Cannot wait and cuts in line or gets impatient when standing in a queue.
Rushes or cuts in without waiting for their turn in games or board games.
Keeps checking the time or complaining when waiting for their turn at hospitals or public offices.
Fidgets, complains, or gets annoyed in situations where waiting for a turn is required.

S018.name: Interrupting_Intruding
S018.description: Often interrupts or intrudes on others (e.g., butts into conversations, games, or activities).
examples: Butts into conversations of others where they have not been invited.
Joins in on others' work or games without permission or interferes.
Touches or uses other people's belongings or work without permission.
Keeps talking to and disturbing others when they are focusing on work or studying.

symptom.disease_info: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation) is characterized by a persistent pattern of both inattention and hyperactive-impulsive behaviors that are inconsistent with developmental level and cause impairment in at least two settings (e.g., work, home, social). Symptoms typically begin in childhood, but in many adults they are only recognized later when occupational, relational, or organizational demands exceed their coping strategies. The course is usually chronic, with fluctuations in severity depending on structure, stress, and environmental supports; some individuals develop compensatory routines that partially mask difficulties until these are overwhelmed. Clinically, it is distinguished from mood, anxiety, and personality disorders by its early onset, pervasiveness across situations, and a core pattern of attentional disorganization and impulse-control difficulties rather than episodic changes in mood or solely situational stress responses.

patient.stressor: In the past two years, Dennis’s call center transitioned to stricter performance metrics and a new omnichannel CRM platform that required rapidly switching between phone, chat, and email while following detailed scripts and documentation protocols. The faster pace and constant dashboard alerts made it increasingly difficult for him to keep his place in workflows, remember what he had just agreed to with a customer, and complete tickets accurately, leading to repeated quality flags and tense coaching sessions despite his strong interpersonal skills and product knowledge. The stress began to spill over into his home life; he would intend to tackle simple tasks like organizing bills or finishing DIY projects after work but instead bounced between unfinished chores, leaving his wife to quietly pick up the slack. When he was placed on a performance improvement plan and told that another quarter of documentation errors could jeopardize his job, Dennis, worried about losing their main source of income before retirement, agreed to an employee assistance referral and then pursued a full psychiatric assessment.
patient.chief_complaint: “At work my mind jumps to every little thing going on around me, and I lose track of what I’m doing in the middle of a customer call.”

S001.name: Detail_Inattention_Errors
S001.description: Often fails to give close attention to details or makes careless mistakes.
S001.manifestation: On the calls, I’ll think I’ve documented everything, but then my supervisor shows me I clicked the wrong box or typed the wrong account number because I just skimmed the screen and rushed instead of really reading it line by line.

S002.name: Sustained_Attention_Difficulty
S002.description: Often has difficulty sustaining attention in tasks or play activities.
S002.manifestation: I can start a customer email or even a simple training video feeling focused, but within a few minutes my brain just drifts off and I realize I’ve either been staring at the screen or typing nonsense without really following what I’m supposed to be doing.

S004.name: Instruction_Follow through_Difficulty
S004.description: Often does not follow through on instructions and fails to finish schoolwork, chores, or duties in the workplace.
S004.manifestation: My manager will give me a clear list of steps for a ticket, and I’ll do the first part and maybe the second, then I get sidetracked by another alert or thought and end up closing the case without finishing the last things she asked for.

S008.name: Distractibility
S008.description: Often easily distracted by extraneous stimuli (for older adolescents and adults, may include unrelated thoughts).
S008.manifestation: During a call, the little pop‑up alerts on the dashboard, people talking a few desks over, or even just a random thought about what I need to buy at the store yank my attention away so fast that I lose my place in the script and have to ask the customer to repeat themselves.

S009.name: Daily_Activities_Forgetfulness
S009.description: Often forgetful in daily activities (e.g., doing chores, running errands; for older adolescents and adults, returning calls, paying bills, keeping appointments).
S009.manifestation: My wife has to remind me over and over about bills, appointments, or even taking the trash out, because if it’s not right in front of me, I’ll walk past it or forget it completely, and then we get late notices or she ends up doing it herself.

S010.name: Fidgeting
S010.description: Often fidgets with or taps hands or feet or squirms in seat.
S010.manifestation: I’m always jiggling my leg, clicking my pen, or drumming my fingers on the desk during shifts, and even when I tell myself to stop I catch myself doing it again a few seconds later without realizing it.

S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
S012.manifestation: Any time I have to sit still for a long meeting or just wait between calls, I feel this buzzing inside, like I need to get up and pace or do something with my hands, and it makes me feel almost trapped in my own chair.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
S013.manifestation: Even at home when I try to relax, I can’t just sit quietly and read or watch a movie with my wife without talking over it, fiddling with my phone, or getting up to start some other noisy project in the middle.

S014.name: Constant_Activity
S014.description: Is often 'on the go', acting as if 'driven by a motor'.
S014.manifestation: My family jokes that I’m like a wind‑up toy because from the moment I get up I’m bouncing from one thing to the next—checking emails, half‑starting chores, pacing while on the phone—and I only realize at the end of the day that I never actually sat down and rested.

S017.name: Waiting_Turn_Difficulty
S017.description: Often has difficulty waiting his or her turn.
S017.manifestation: Whether it’s standing in line at the grocery store or waiting my turn to speak on a team call, I get so impatient and antsy that I either cut in with what I want to say or start huffing and shifting around because it feels unbearable just to wait.

S018.name: Interrupting_Intruding
S018.description: Often interrupts or intrudes on others (e.g., butts into conversations, games, or activities).
S018.manifestation: I keep catching myself jumping into other people’s conversations at work or finishing their sentences on calls, not because I’m trying to be rude but because the thought pops into my head and comes out of my mouth before I can stop it.

add_requirements.onset_prior_to_12_years: Even back in elementary school my teachers were always moving my seat because I wouldn’t stop talking, tapping my pencil, or staring out the window instead of finishing worksheets, and my report cards kept saying I was smart but ‘doesn’t pay attention’ and ‘rushes and makes careless mistakes.’
add_requirements.functional_impairment: Because I keep missing steps, making documentation errors, and leaving things half-finished at home, my job is now at risk with a performance plan and my wife has to quietly take over more of the bills and chores, which has caused a lot of stress and tension between us.
add_requirements.duration: These problems have really come to a head over the last almost two years, ever since our call center switched to the new fast-paced system and stricter performance tracking.
